label: Some Basic Constructions
notes: This chapter, printed pages 56 through 80, is a toolkit. We learn how to assemble new geodesic spaces from old ones: products, cones, joins, and gluings. The recurring question is which metric features survive each operation, and how the curvature of a construction is governed by the curvature of its pieces.

label: The Product Metric
notes: The l-two product metric combines two spaces by adding squared distances under a square root, exactly as Pythagoras combines coordinate displacements. Stress that geodesics in the product are pairs of factor geodesics traced at proportional speed, and that completeness, geodesicity, and uniqueness of geodesics all transfer factor by factor to the product.

label: Curvature of Products
notes: Products preserve curvature bounds in the non-positive regime: a product of two CAT(0) spaces is CAT(0). Emphasise that the comparison works because a geodesic triangle in the product projects to triangles in each factor, and the squared distances add. Warn that for positive bounds the clean additivity fails, which is why joins replace products there.

label: The Euclidean Cone
notes: The Euclidean cone glues a copy of a half-line to every point of the base, then measures distance using the law of cosines with the base distance read as an angle. Walk through the formula carefully: the angle between two rays is the base distance capped at pi, and the cone is built so apex neighbourhoods record that angle.

label: Cone Over a Circle
notes: This is the signature picture. Coning a circle of circumference L yields a genuine cone whose sharpness encodes L. When L equals two pi the cone unrolls flat to the Euclidean plane; when L is below two pi the apex is positively curved and CAT(0) fails; above two pi the apex carries negative curvature concentration. Make students feel the threshold.

label: The k-Cone
notes: The k-cone generalises the Euclidean cone by building rays inside the model space of curvature k rather than the flat plane. The distance formula uses the law of cosines for that model geometry. For k positive the cone closes up into a sphere-like suspension; this single definition unifies cones, suspensions, and the spherical pieces used later.

label: The Spherical Join
notes: The spherical join interpolates between two spaces by a quarter-circle of joining geodesics, with the join metric built from the spherical law of cosines. Emphasise that the join of spheres is again a sphere of one higher dimension, and that the join is exactly the link, or unit tangent picture, that the k-cone produces at its apex.

label: Cones, Joins, and Curvature
notes: State the central package: the Euclidean cone over X is CAT(0) precisely when X is CAT(1), and the spherical join of two spaces is CAT(1) precisely when both factors are. These two theorems convert a curvature bound on a small link into a curvature bound on the big cone, and they preview Berestovskii and the link condition.

label: Quotient Pseudometrics
notes: Gluing is run through the quotient pseudometric: the distance between two classes is the infimum over chains of admissible jumps and in-piece paths. Explain that the result is only a pseudometric in general, that collapsing the zero-distance relation makes it a genuine metric, and that this infimum-over-chains formula is the engine behind every gluing in the book.

label: Gluing Along Subspaces
notes: When two spaces are glued along an isometric copy of a common subspace, the quotient metric restricts isometrically to each piece and to the seam. Reshetnyak's gluing lemma guarantees geodesics either stay in one piece or cross the seam once. This is how trees, complexes, and developments of polygons are assembled metrically.

label: Warped and Twisted Products
notes: Warped products rescale the second factor by a positive function on the first, so the metric reads as base distance plus warped fibre distance. These twisted products produce hyperbolic space as a warped product of a line and a horosphere, and they let curvature be redistributed; flag that survival of bounds now depends on the warping function.

label: Survival Map and Recap
notes: Close with the survival ledger from the notebook: track geodesic existence, completeness, and the curvature input across products, cones, joins, and gluings. The single transferable lesson is that each construction has an explicit distance formula, and every curvature claim is checked by feeding comparison triangles into that formula.
